BURHAN:v3p34/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p34/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p34/r3.claim: The augmented form واصطبر conveys a stronger command than أصبر.
BURHAN:v3p34/r3.anchor: فإنه أبلغ من الأمر بالصبر من أصبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r1.claim: The good outcome, or praiseworthy end, belongs to the God-fearing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p401/r1.anchor: والعاقبة أي الحميدة أو حسن العاقبة لأهل التقوى

FARRA:v2p196/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p196/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p196/r4.claim: لا نسألك رزقا means God does not ask people for payment; رزق ربك means your Lord's reward.
FARRA:v2p196/r4.anchor: أجرا على ذلك. وكذلك قوله (ورزق ربك) يريد: وثواب ربك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r12.claim: The Prophet is to command his household to pray, as his forefather Ishmael did, so he leads them to every good; teaching others purifies sincerity.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r12.anchor: كما كان أبوك إسماعيل عليه السلام , ليقودهم إلى كل خير

TABATABAI:20:127-135/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r3.claim: A report says that after the command to pray, the Prophet came to Ali's doorway for eight months, urging prayer and reciting the purification verse; another version says nine months.
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r3.anchor: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يجيء إلى باب علي

TABATABAI:20:127-135/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r4.speaker: أبو الحميراء
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r4.claim: Abu al-Hamra says he witnessed the Prophet visit Ali and Fatima's door for forty mornings, greet the Household, and urge prayer.
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r4.anchor: شهدت النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أربعين صباحا يجيء إلى باب علي وفاطمة فيأخذ بعضادتي الباب ثم يقول السلام عليكم أهل البيت

TABATABAI:20:127-135/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r5.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says reports giving nine months reflect the witness's observation rather than a fixed duration; their apparent Medinan setting is difficult for a Meccan verse, though one report describes visits in Medina.
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r5.anchor: التقييد بتسعة أشهر مبني على ما شاهده الراوي لا على تحديد أصل إتيانه

TABATABAI:20:127-135/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r6.claim: When hardship or poverty struck his household, the Prophet told them to pray and recited this verse.
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r6.anchor: إذا نزلت بأهله شدة أو ضيق أمرهم بالصلاة

TABATABAI:20:127-135/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r7.claim: Reports that the Prophet directed his family to pray during hardship, including reports from Thabit, show that the verse's glorification can be understood broadly to include prayer.
TABATABAI:20:127-135/r7.anchor: وفيه دلالة على التوسع في معنى التسبيح في الآية

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p66/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p66/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p66/r1.claim: The Prophet’s preaching does not depend on opponents’ wealth or patronage; God sustains him and his companions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p66/r1.anchor: God is his patron and sufficient to sustain him and his companions

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r5.claim: Ahl has a wider Arabic meaning than the Prophet's household: it includes people related to someone and can denote a prophet's nation, as shown by lexicography and usage.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r6.speaker: Abu Bakr (rta)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r6.claim: A report from Abū Bakr uses ahl broadly: when asked whom he appointed over Muslims, he answered that he appointed the best ahl.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r6.anchor: Abu Bakr (rta) that when on the day of Judgement his Lord

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r7.claim: Ismāʿīl's command to his ahl to observe prayer and zakāh means those associated with him, not only his wife and children.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p86/r7.anchor: all those associated to him are meant.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r1.claim: In this verse ahl includes every believer in Muḥammad, whether kin or not, Quraysh or Hashimite, enslaved or free, man or woman; this use raises the standing of poor Muslims as the Prophet's family.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r1.anchor: Muslims regardless of belonging to the Quraysh or the Hashimites

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r2.claim: The Prophet must maintain prayer and direct his followers to do likewise; this is the vigilant prayer already described in the preceding verse, which builds perseverance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r2.anchor: The prayer here refers to the same prayer mentioned in the previous verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r3.claim: The command to persevere in prayer pictures a farmer tilling, sowing, watering, and guarding his land until it yields blessings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r3.anchor: just as a farmer tills his soil, sows deeds, waters it and continues to guard it, the Prophet (sws) too should tend to his land

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r4.claim: God promises livelihood to the Prophet and his followers so he can continue his task and prayer without anxiety about provision; Jesus is reported to say that a laborer deserves his hire.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r4.anchor: Jesus (sws) is reported to have said: “The labourer is worthy of his hire.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r5.claim: The singular pronoun for God's providing for the Prophet addresses him as head of the whole Muslim family, so the promise includes all Muslims; in the Islamic political system the ruler provides for the community.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r5.anchor: This address to the Prophet (sws) is in his capacity of the head of the Islamic family and its sustainer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r6.claim: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar exemplified responsibility for their people; ʿUmar felt accountable even if a dog died hungry in a distant part of his realm and acted to prevent such suffering.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r6.anchor: did not merely express these emotions but took practical steps

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r7.claim: After promising worldly sustenance, the verse gives the Hereafter's glad tidings: only the pious attain ultimate success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p87/r7.anchor: In the previous part of the verse, promise for worldly sustenance was made; now glad tidings of success in the hereafter are given

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r1.claim: Prayer's guarantee of provision cannot be conveyed to those who lack its true experience; only people who taste its essence can know what it contains, and Islahi says he has seen devout examples in life and history.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p88/r1.anchor: Only experience can convince a person

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r4.claim: Some take “your family” as relatives, but Rāzī prefers all followers of the Prophet's religion, paralleling 19:55; he also allows the household residents, whom he could remind of prayer at its times.

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r5.claim: Rāzī allows “your family” to mean those who live in the house, since they can be reminded of the prayer at its appointed times; as God ordered the Prophet, he should order his people.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r5.anchor: وإن احتمل أن يكون المراد من يضمه المسكن إذ التنبيه على الصلاة والأمر بها في أوقاتها ممكن فيهم دون سائر الأمة

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r6.claim: The Prophet should maintain prayer in practice as he commands it, since preaching by one's actions is more complete than preaching by words.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r6.anchor: فحافظ عليها فعلا ، فإن الوعظ بلسان الفعل أتم

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r7.claim: Rāzī reports that after this verse was revealed, the Prophet visited Fāṭima and ʿAlī every morning, called them to prayer, and continued for months.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r7.anchor: صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد نزول هذه الآية يذهب إلى فاطمة

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r8.claim: Rāzī says the command to pray serves people's benefit; God is above needing any benefit from their worship.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r8.anchor: ثم بين تعالى أنه إنما يأمرهم بذلك لمنافعهم وأنه متعال عن المنافع

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r9.claim: Abū Muslim says God seeks worship from the Prophet and people, not their provision as masters demand tribute from slaves, paralleling 51:56–57.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r9.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : المعنى أنه تعالى إنما يريد منه ومنهم العبادة

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r10.claim: Another explanation is that God does not ask the Prophet or his family to provide for themselves; God provides for them so he can devote his attention to the afterlife, as the saying goes, whoever works for God has God attend to his work.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r10.anchor: لنفسك ولا لأهلك بل نحن نرزقك ونرزق أهلك ، ففرغ بالك لأمر الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r11.claim: A third explanation is that God gains nothing from the commanded prayer: He provides worldly blessings and hereafter reward instead.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r11.anchor: بل نحن نرزقك في الدنيا بوجوه النعم وفي الآخرة بالثواب

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r12.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām reports that whenever hardship or distress came upon the Prophet's family, he told them to pray and recited this verse.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r12.anchor: قال عبد الله بن سلام : ( كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r13.claim: The verse does not permit abandoning livelihood, since the pious are described as people whom trade and sale do not distract from remembering God.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r13.anchor: واعلم أنه ليس في الآية رخصة في ترك التكسب لأنه تعالى قال في وصف المتقين

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r14.claim: The beautiful final outcome belongs to those who fear God.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r14.anchor: والعاقبة للتقوى فالمراد والعاقبة الجميلة لأهل التقوى

RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r15.claim: After the counsel on patience and prayer, Rāzī reads the following account of the opponents' objection as continuing the instruction to endure what they say in 20:130.
RAZI-FULL:v22p118/r15.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه بعد هذه الوصية حكى عنهم شبهتهم

STUDYQURAN:20:132/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r1.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r1.claim: One view takes “family” (ahl) to mean the Prophet’s close relatives.

STUDYQURAN:20:132/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r2.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r2.claim: Another view takes ahl to mean the people of the Prophet’s faith, hence “thy people”; ahl can mean either family or people.
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r2.anchor: while others say that it refers to the people of his faith (R), in which case thy family would be rendered “thy people” instead

STUDYQURAN:20:132/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r3.claim: Although the command addresses the Prophet, it applies to believers generally.
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r3.anchor: Although this injunction is addressed to the Prophet, it applies to the believers in general (Q)

STUDYQURAN:20:132/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r4.claim: The assurance that God provides is compared with 51:57–58, where God says He seeks no provision from people.
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r4.anchor: We ask no provision of thee; We provide for thee is similar to 51:57–58

STUDYQURAN:20:132/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r5.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r5.claim: The end belonging to reverence means that Paradise is for the reverent.
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r5.anchor: the end belongs to reverence means that Paradise is for those who are reverent (see 2:2c; JJ)

STUDYQURAN:20:132/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r6.claim: Other Qurʾānic passages also say that the end belongs to the reverent.
STUDYQURAN:20:132/r6.anchor: Elsewhere in the Quran, it also says that the end belongs to the reverent (7:128; 11:49; 28:83)

TAB-FULL:v16p213/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r5.speaker: أبو رافع
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r5.claim: In another Abu Rafi report, a Jewish lender required a pledge after a guest arrived; the Prophet offered his armor, and verses 15:87 and 20:131–132 were revealed.
TAB-FULL:v16p213/r5.anchor: عن أبي رافع، قال: نزل برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيف: فأرسلني إلى يهودي بالمدينة يستسلفه، فأتيته

TAB-FULL:v16p216/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p216/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p216/r1.claim: The Prophet must command his household to pray and patiently keep up prayer himself, performing it with its prescribed limits.
TAB-FULL:v16p216/r1.anchor: لا نسألك مالا، بل نكلفك عملا ببدنك

TAB-FULL:v16p216/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p216/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p216/r2.claim: God asks the Prophet for bodily work, not wealth, promises a great reward for it, and provides wealth Himself.
TAB-FULL:v16p216/r2.anchor: نحن نعطيك المال ونكسبكه، ولا نسألكه

TAB-FULL:v16p217/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p217/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p217/r1.claim: The good final outcome of every person's deeds belongs to the God-fearing, not those who fear no punishment or hope for no reward.
TAB-FULL:v16p217/r1.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، قال: كان عروة إذا رأى ما عند السلاطين دخل داره

TAB-FULL:v16p217/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p217/r2.speaker: عروة
TAB-FULL:v16p217/r2.claim: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa reports that when ʿUrwa saw the rulers' worldly goods, he went home, recited these verses, and called his family to prayer.
TAB-FULL:v16p217/r2.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، قال: كان عروة إذا رأى ما عند السلاطين دخل داره، فقال

TAB-FULL:v16p217/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p217/r3.speaker: عروة
TAB-FULL:v16p217/r3.claim: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa also reports that when ʿUrwa saw something worldly, he went to his family and told them to pray.
TAB-FULL:v16p217/r3.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، أنه كان إذا رأى شيئا من الدنيا جاء إلى أهله، فقال: الصلاة

TABATABAI:20:131-132/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r4.claim: This verse is Meccan like the rest of the sūra; the author finds no authority who exempts it as Medinan.
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r4.anchor: الآية ذات سياق يلتئم بسياق سائر آيات السورة فهي مكية كسائرها على أنا لم نظفر بمن يستثنيها

TABATABAI:20:131-132/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r5.claim: At the time of revelation, the Prophet's household refers to Khadīja and ʿAlī, who lived in his household, possibly together with some of his daughters.
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r5.anchor: وعلى هذا فالمراد بقوله { أهلك } بحسب انطباقه على وقت النزول خديجة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:20:131-132/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r6.claim: Some identify the household as the Prophet's wives and daughters and his son-in-law ʿAlī.
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r6.anchor: فقول بعضهم إن المراد به أزواجه وبناته وصهره علي،

TABATABAI:20:131-132/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī accepts that first view as a continuing application, not as the Meccan occasion of revelation, when Khadīja was the Prophet's only wife there.
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r7.anchor: نعم لا بأس بالقول الأول من حيث جري الآية وانطباقها لا من حيث مورد النزول

TABATABAI:20:131-132/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r8.speaker: آخرين
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r8.claim: Others include the Prophet's wives and daughters and relatives from Banū Hāshim and al-Muṭṭalib; the author rejects this as the intended referent.
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r8.anchor: وقول آخرين المراد به أزواجه وبناته وأقرباؤه من بني هاشم والمطلب،

TABATABAI:20:131-132/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r9.speaker: آخرين
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r9.claim: Another view takes the household to mean all followers of the Muslim community; the author calls this unsound.
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r9.anchor: وقول آخرين جميع متبعيه من أمته غير سديد

TABATABAI:20:131-132/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r10.claim: The contrast means God does not ask the Prophet to provide Him with sustenance: God is independent, while people depend on Him for provision.
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r10.anchor: ظاهر المقابلة بين الجملتين أن المراد سؤاله تعالى الرزق لنفسه وهو كناية عن أنا في غنى منك

TABATABAI:20:131-132/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r11.claim: The ending echoes 22:37, where the verse says sacrificial meat and blood do not reach God, but piety does.
TABATABAI:20:131-132/r11.anchor: وأيضا هو من جهة تذييله بقوله { والعاقبة للتقوى } في معنى قوله

TABATABAI:20:132-133/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r1.claim: The author rejects interpreting God's request as asking for provision for creatures or for the Prophet himself.
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r1.anchor: فتفسيرهم سؤال الرزق بسؤال الرزق للخلق أو لنفس النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ليس بسديد

TABATABAI:20:132-133/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r2.claim: The author says the outcome belonging to piety has been discussed repeatedly.
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r2.anchor: وقوله { والعاقبة للتقوى } تقدم البحث فيه كرارا.

TABATABAI:20:132-133/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r3.claim: The family prayer command, alongside prior orders for the Prophet's daily prayers and patience and the warning against gazing at unbelievers' goods, suggests an early Meccan date for the sūra or verse.
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r3.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يستفاد من الآية من جهة قصر الأمر بالصلاة في أهله مع ما في الآيتين السابقتين

TABATABAI:20:132-133/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿūd describes Sūrat Ṭā Hā as one of the earliest old sūras.
TABATABAI:20:132-133/r4.anchor: وفيما روي عن ابن مسعود أن سورة طه من العتاق الأول

TABRISI:20:132-135/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:132-135/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to command his household and the people of his religion to pray.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r1.anchor: معناه وأمر يا محمد أهل بيتك وأهل دينك بالصلاة

TABRISI:20:132-135/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
TABRISI:20:132-135/r2.claim: For nine months after this verse was revealed, the Prophet went to Fatima and Ali’s door at every prayer and called the household to prayer, invoking the household-purification verse.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r2.anchor: روى أبو سعيد الخدري قال لما نزلت هذه الآية كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يأتي باب فاطمة وعلي تسعة أشهر

TABRISI:20:132-135/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r3.speaker: ابن عقدة
TABRISI:20:132-135/r3.claim: Ibn Uqda transmitted the report through many chains from the Prophet’s household and others, including Abu Barza and Abu Rafi.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r3.anchor: ورواه ابن عقدة بإسناده من طرق كثيرة عن أهل البيت ع وعن غيرهم مثل أبي برزة وأبي رافع

TABRISI:20:132-135/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:20:132-135/r4.claim: God specifically commanded Muhammad to single out his family, so people would know their standing with God; they were first included in the general command, then addressed specially.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r4.anchor: أمره الله تعالى أن يخص أهله دون الناس ليعلم الناس أن لأهله عند الله منزلة

TABRISI:20:132-135/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:132-135/r5.claim: Persevere in performing prayer and in commanding the family to perform it.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r5.anchor: أي واصبر على فعلها وعلى أمرهم بها

TABRISI:20:132-135/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:132-135/r6.claim: God does not ask provision for His creatures or for Himself; He charged the Prophet with worship and conveying the message and guaranteed everyone’s provision.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r6.anchor: لخلقنا ولا لنفسك بل كلفناك العبادة وأداء الرسالة وضمنا رزق الجميع

TABRISI:20:132-135/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:132-135/r7.claim: Although addressed to the Prophet, the promise means God provides for all people and neither seeks nor benefits from their provision.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r7.anchor: الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد به جميع الخلق أي نرزق جميعهم ولا نسترزقهم

TABRISI:20:132-135/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:132-135/r8.claim: The praiseworthy final outcome belongs to the people who fear God.

TABRISI:20:132-135/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:132-135/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse means those who affirmed the Prophet, followed him, and feared God.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد الذين صدقوك واتبعوك واتقوني

TABRISI:20:132-135/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:132-135/r10.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
TABRISI:20:132-135/r10.claim: An account says Urwa ibn al-Zubayr would go home when he saw what the ruler had, recite the warning against coveting worldly goods, then call his household to prayer.
TABRISI:20:132-135/r10.anchor: وفي الأثر أن عروة الزبير كان إذا رأى ما عند السلطان دخل بيته وقرأ ولا تمدن عينيك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r1.claim: A report says that after this verse was revealed, the Prophet visited ʿAlī and Fāṭima each morning for several months and called them to prayer; no grading is stated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r1.anchor: - قوله تعالى: {وأمر أهلك بالصلاة} روي: (أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية كان رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r2.claim: Here “your family” means the Prophet’s people and those who share his religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى الأهل هاهنا: قومه ومن كان على دينه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r3.claim: The commentary refers to its earlier explanation of the verse saying that he commanded his family to pray.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r4.claim: Persevere in prayer to help resist God’s prohibitions, since prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r4.anchor: {واصطبر عليها} للاستعانة على الصبر عن محارم الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r5.claim: Ibn Muslim says God does not ask the Prophet to provide sustenance for His creation or for Himself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن مسلم: (لا نسألك رزقا لخلقنا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r6.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām says that when the Prophet’s household faced hardship, he told them to pray and recited this verse; no grading is stated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p562#2/r6.anchor: قال عبد الله بن سلام: (كان النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- إذا أنزل بأهله ضيق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddī identify the final outcome as Paradise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563/r1.anchor: وقوله: {والعاقبة} قال ابن عباس، والسدي: (يريد: بالعاقبة الجنة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563/r2.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash explains li-l-taqwā as “for the people of piety.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {للتقوى} قال الأخفش: (أي لأهل التقوى)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the pious as those who believed the Prophet, followed him, and feared God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p563/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: الذين صدقوك واتبعوك واتقوني)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r1.claim: The family ordered to pray means Quraysh.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r2.claim: Another view says the family ordered to pray means the Prophet's household.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r3.claim: God does not ask sustenance for His creation or for Himself; He provides for them.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r4.claim: The ultimate outcome is Paradise, for the God-fearing—meaning the Prophet and those who believe him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r4.anchor: الجنة { للتقوى } لأهل التقوى. يعني: لك ولمن صدقك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r5.claim: These verses were revealed when the Messenger borrowed from a Jewish man, who insisted on collateral before lending, and the Messenger was saddened.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:132-134/r5.anchor: لما استسلف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من يهودي وأبى أن يعطيه إلا برهن، وحزن لذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r5.claim: The Prophet's family here means his community.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r5.anchor: وأمر أهلك بالصلاة} [طه: 132] وأهله في هذا الموضع: أمته.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r6.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r6.claim: Some say God does not ask provision from the Prophet in return for the prophethood bestowed on him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم: لا نسألك على ما أعطيناك من النبوة رزقا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r7.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r7.claim: Al-Hasan's gloss on 51:57 is that God does not want people to provide for themselves.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r7.anchor: وتفسير الحسن في التي في الذاريات: {ما أريد منهم من رزق} [الذاريات: 57] أن يرزقوا أنفسهم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r8.claim: If al-Hasan's reading carries over, God is not asking the Prophet to provide for himself; Yahya prefers this reading.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r8.anchor: قال يحيى: فإن كانت هذه عند الحسن مثلها فهو: {لا نسألك رزقا} [طه: 132] أن ترزق نفسك وهو أعجب إلي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r9.claim: The good end belongs to the people of piety.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r9.anchor: قال يحيى: {نحن نرزقك والعاقبة للتقوى} [طه: 132] أي: لأهل التقوى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r10.claim: He identifies the good end as Paradise, as in 43:35, where the Hereafter is for the pious.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p295/r10.anchor: والعاقبة: الجنة كقوله: {والآخرة عند ربك للمتقين} [الزخرف: 35]

QASHANI:20:131-133/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:131-133/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:131-133/r3.claim: The family signifies spiritual and psychic faculties directed to presence, vigilance, obedience, and responsiveness; perseverance means spiritual struggle and unveiling.
QASHANI:20:131-133/r3.anchor: { وأمر أهلك } القوى الروحانية والنفسانية بصلاة الحضور والمراقبة والانقياد والمطاوعة { واصطبر } على تلك الحالة بالمجاهدة والمكاشفة

QASHANI:20:131-133/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:131-133/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:131-133/r4.claim: God does not ask for lower-world perfections or sensory knowledge; He provides higher spiritual knowledge and holy realities.
QASHANI:20:131-133/r4.anchor: { لا نسألك } لا نطلب منك { رزقا } من الجهة السفلية كالكمالات الحسية والمدركات النفسية { نحن نرزقك } من الجهة العلوية المعارف الروحانية

QASHANI:20:131-133/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:131-133/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:131-133/r5.claim: The true worthy outcome is detachment from bodily garments and psychic dispositions.
QASHANI:20:131-133/r5.anchor: { والعاقبة } التي تعتبر وتستأهل أن تسمى عاقبة للتجرد عن الملابس البدنية والهيئات النفسانية

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r6.claim: Prayer opens the door of provision and is the means God directs people to when they need a breakthrough.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r6.anchor: الصلاة استفتاح باب الرزق ، وعليها أحال في تيسير الفتوح عند وقوع الحاجة إليه

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r7.claim: Prayer is nourishment and healing for hearts; when the soul's nourishment is delayed, the heart's nourishment grows stronger.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r7.anchor: الصلاة رزق القلوب ، وفيها شفاؤها ، وإذا استأخر قوت النفس قوي قوت القلب

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r8.claim: Istiṣbār has an added quality over patience: its practitioner feels no pain but is carried and comforted through it.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r8.anchor: وللاصطبار مزية على الصبر ؛ وهو ألا يجد صاحبه الألم بل يكون محمولا مروحا

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r9.claim: God does not charge the Prophet with providing anyone; God alone provides for him and everyone, without creatures having causal power over provision.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r9.anchor: لا نكلفك برزق أحد ، فإن الرازق الله - سبحانه - دون تأثير الخلق ، فنحن نرزقك ونرزق الجميع

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r10.claim: There are two matters: having provisions strengthens souls, while witnessing the Provider strengthens hearts.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r10.anchor: هما شيئان : وجود الأرزاق وشهود الرزاق ؛ فوجود الأرزاق يوجب قوة النفوس ، وشهود الرزاق يوجب قوة القلوب

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r11.claim: Ordinary people are sustained by the existence of provisions, whereas the elect are sustained by witnessing the Provider.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r11.anchor: ويقال استقلال العامة بوجود الأرزاق ، واستقلال الخواص بشهود الرزاق

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r12.claim: Whoever realizes the divine 'We' no longer distinguishes one provision from another.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r12.anchor: فإن من شهد وتحقق بقوله : { نحن } سقط عنه التمييز بين رزق ورزق

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r13.claim: The promise 'We provide' consoles the poor when provision is scarce or delayed.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r13.anchor: خففف على الفقراء مقاساة قلة الرزق وتأخره عن وقت إلى وقت بقوله : { نحن }

QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r14.claim: The good end belongs to the people of piety; the word for piety may also designate the pious person by naming the one described with the verbal noun.
QUSHAYRI:v2p282/r14.anchor: العاقبة بالحسنى لأهل التقوى . ويقال المراد بالتقوى المتقي ، فقد يسمى الموصوف بما هو المصدر

SULAMI:v1p453#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r1.claim: The prohibition on admiring worldly life consoles the poor; the next command turns them toward worship and perseverance in prayer.
SULAMI:v1p453#4/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه في هذه الآية : تسلية للفقراء وتعزية لهم حيث منع الخلق عن النظر إلى الدنيا على وجه الإستحسان فقال :

SULAMI:v2p3#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r1.claim: The greatest steadfastness is remaining inwardly still under trials in one's secret, heart, and self; ordinary patience pertains only to the self.
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أشد أنواع الصبر الاصطبار ، وهو السكون تحت موارد البلاء بالسر ، والقلب ، والنفس ،

SULAMI:v2p3#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r2.claim: Commanding one's family to pray means commanding them to join God and patiently maintain that connection, something only the divinely supported can bear.
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r2.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه في قوله : ﴿ وأمر أهلك بالصلاة ﴾ قال : وأمر أهلك بالاتصال بنا ،

SULAMI:v2p3#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r3.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r3.claim: Worshippers wear garments bestowed by God, with prayer as their warp and fasting as their weft.
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r3.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ : للعابدين أردية يكسونها من عند الله سداؤها الصلاة ولحمتها الصوم .

SULAMI:v2p3#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r4.claim: Learning prayer means being present of heart.

SULAMI:v2p3#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r5.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r5.claim: The outcome for the God-fearing is disciplining the self and limbs away from everything knowledge does not permit.
SULAMI:v2p3#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : هو ذم النفس والجوارح من جميع ما لا يبيحه بالعلم

ITQAN:v1p262/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p262/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p262/r1.claim: Hamza is difficult to articulate, and Quraysh and the Hijaz most often used its softened forms; this is frequent in Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ through Warsh, and Abū ʿAmr.
ITQAN:v1p262/r1.anchor: اعلم أن الهمز لما كان أثقل الحروف نطقا وأبعدها مخرجا تنوع العرب في تخفيفه بأنواع التخفيف

ITQAN:v1p262/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p262/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
ITQAN:v1p262/r2.claim: A report through Nāfiʿ claims that the Prophet, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and the caliphs did not pronounce hamza and that later people introduced it.
ITQAN:v1p262/r2.anchor: عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال ما همز رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا أبو بكر ولا عمر ولا الخلفاء

ITQAN:v1p262/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p262/r3.speaker: أبو شامة
ITQAN:v1p262/r3.claim: Abū Shāma rejects that report as unusable evidence because Mūsā b. ʿUbayda al-Rabadhī is weak among hadith critics.
ITQAN:v1p262/r3.anchor: قال أبو شامة هذا حديث لا يحتج به وموسى بن عبيدة الربذي ضعيف عند أئمة الحديث

ITQAN:v1p262/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p262/r4.speaker: أبو ذر
ITQAN:v1p262/r4.claim: A report says a Bedouin addressed the Prophet as “O prophet of God”; the Prophet replied that he was nabī Allāh, not nabīʾ Allāh.
ITQAN:v1p262/r4.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال جاء أعرابي إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا نبيء الله فقال لست بنبيء الله ولكني نبي الله

ITQAN:v1p262/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p262/r5.speaker: الذهبي
ITQAN:v1p262/r5.claim: Al-Dhahabī calls the Abū Dharr report anomalous and says Ḥumrān is a Rāfiḍī and not trustworthy.
ITQAN:v1p262/r5.anchor: قال الذهبي حديث منكر وحمران رافضي ليس بثقة

ITQAN:v1p262/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p262/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p262/r6.claim: The chapter selects four broad kinds of hamza treatment for discussion, although this excerpt details only the first two.
ITQAN:v1p262/r6.anchor: والذي نورده هنا أن تحقيقه أربعة أنواع

ITQAN:v1p262/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p262/r7.speaker: نافع
ITQAN:v1p262/r7.claim: In naql, the hamza's vowel moves to a preceding final consonant that is still; the hamza then drops, as in “qad aflaḥa,” read by Nāfiʿ through Warsh.
ITQAN:v1p262/r7.anchor: أحدها النقل لحركته إلى الساكن قبله فيسقط نحو

ITQAN:v1p262/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p262/r8.speaker: أصحاب يعقوب عن ورش
ITQAN:v1p262/r8.claim: An exception is “kitābiyah innī ẓanantu”: Yaʿqūb's transmitters from Warsh leave hāʾ still and retain the hamza; other readers retain hamza throughout.
ITQAN:v1p262/r8.anchor: واستثنى أصحاب يعقوب عن ورش ﴿ كتابيه إني ظننت ﴾ فسكنوا الهاء وحققوا الهمزة

ITQAN:v1p262/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p262/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو
ITQAN:v1p262/r9.claim: In ibdāl, a still hamza becomes a long vowel matching the preceding vowel; Abū ʿAmr reads this way whether hamza is initial, medial, or final.
ITQAN:v1p262/r9.anchor: وثانيها الإبدال بأن تبدل الهمزة الساكنة حرف مد من جنس حركة ما قبلها

ITQAN:v1p262/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p262/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p262/r10.claim: Hamza is retained under jussive or construct-state stillness, and where dropping it would be harder or cause ambiguity; moving hamza is always verified.
ITQAN:v1p262/r10.anchor: إلا أن يكون سكونها جزما نحو / ننسأها / أو بناء نحو / أرجئه /

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r1.claim: Hyperbolic praise may use seemingly harsh language, as in calling the praised man a rope, a well, or feverish from thinking of virtues; the words need not be read as literal insult.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r1.anchor: وإذا ما أردت كنت رشاء وإذا ما أردت كنت قليبا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r2.speaker: النبي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r2.claim: The Prophet’s report that Islam will reach wherever night reaches illustrates night’s universal reach without requiring its darkness to be part of the comparison.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r2.anchor: فقد جاء في الخبر عن النبي ليدخلن هذا الدين ما دخل عليه الليل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r3.claim: Both day and night reach every place, but choosing night can signal that the pursued person is evading a resentful pursuer; the author treats this as a possible defense of that reading.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r3.anchor: اختصاصه الليل دليل على أنه قد روى في نفسه فلما علم أن حالة إدراكه وقد هرب منه حالة سخط

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r4.claim: A favorable quality should closely serve the simile’s purpose, as the sun suits a welcome blessing; an unfavorable feature may be incidental and left unexamined.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p220/r4.anchor: لأن الصفة المحبوبة إذا اتصلت بالغرض من التشبيه نالت من العناية بها والمحافظة عليها قريبا مما يناله الغرض نفسه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r1.claim: In ordinary usage, ahl means relatives by blood who are bound by kinship and mutual support; by contextual indication it can be used figuratively.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r1.anchor: الأهل في عموم التعارف : الأقارب من العصبة وذوي الأرحام

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r3.claim: The lexical note also gives ihāla as melted fat and says istaʾhala al-rajul means he ate it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r3.anchor: والإهالة : للودك المذاب . وأستأهل الرجل : أكلها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r10.claim: In the command to establish prayer at home, ahl means the community or household under one’s care.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r10.anchor: والسابع : الأمة . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#9/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#9/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#9/r1.claim: God does not ask the Prophet to provide for His creatures or to provide for himself.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#9/r1.anchor: {لا نسألك رزقا} أي لا نسألك رزقا لخلقنا، ولا رزقا لنفسك.

SAMIN-DURR:20:132/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:132/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:132/r1.claim: للتقوى means for the people of piety, supported by the parallel statement that the outcome belongs to the pious.
SAMIN-DURR:20:132/r1.anchor: أي: لأهل التقوى. ويؤيد هذا قوله في موضع أخر

SAMIN-DURR:20:132/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:132/r2.speaker: ابن وثاب
SAMIN-DURR:20:132/r2.claim: Ibn Waththāb assimilates the qāf of نرزقك into the kāf; his usual practice is to assimilate only when the kāf joins a plural mīm, as in 2:21.
SAMIN-DURR:20:132/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب " نرزقك " بإدغام القاف في الكاف.

ASAD-NOTES:20:132#n117/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:132#n117/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:20:132#n117/r1.claim: Razi reads the sentence as saying prayer benefits people alone, since God is exalted above any need of benefits; Asad's “for Us” interpolation follows this reading.
ASAD-NOTES:20:132#n117/r1.anchor: Razi's interpretation of the above sentence: "God makes it clear that He has enjoined this [i.e., prayer] upon men for their own benefit alone

ASAD-NOTES:20:132#n117/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:132#n117/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:132#n117/r2.claim: Asad says prayer is a spiritual benefit for the worshipper, not a tribute owed to a jealous God, a portrayal he associates with the Old Testament in its present corrupted form.
ASAD-NOTES:20:132#n117/r2.anchor: prayer must not be conceived as a kind of tribute to a "jealous God"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p593/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p593/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p593/r3.claim: He poses, without answering in this excerpt, the difference between the command to keep one's own self steadfast and to persist in prayer with one's family.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p593/r3.anchor: ما الفرق من الناحية البيانية بين قوله تعالى

NASHR:v2p322/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r1.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر
NASHR:v2p322/r1.claim: In إنك لا, Nafi and Abu Bakr read the hamza with kasra; the remaining readers use fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p322/r1.anchor: فقرأ نافع وأبو بكر بكسر الهمزة، وقرأ الباقون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r14.claim: After commanding praise at the appointed times and warning against coveting unbelievers' wealth, God commands the Prophet to order his household to pray and persevere through prayer's demands; the address also includes his community.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r14.anchor: أمره تعالى بأن يأمر أهله بالصلاة التي هي بعد الشهادة آكد أركان الإسلام، وأمره بالاصطبار على مداومتها ومشاقها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r15.claim: God does not require the Prophet to provide for himself or exhaust himself pursuing livelihood; He provides, freeing him to attend to the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r15.anchor: وأخبره تعالى أن لا يسأله أن يرزق نفسه وأن لا يسعى في تحصيل الرزق ويدأب في ذلك، بل أمره بتفريغ باله لأمر الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r16.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r16.claim: The majority read نرزقك with a ḍamm on the qāf.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r17.speaker: فرقة وابن وثاب ويعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r17.claim: A group including Ibn Waththāb, and also Yaʿqūb, assimilates the qāf into the kāf; al-Lawāmiʿ explains why Abū ʿAmr avoids assimilation at a word-final consonant and how assimilating readers account for that position.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r17.anchor: وقرأت فرقة: منهم وابن وثاب بإدغام القاف في الكاف وجاء ذلك عن يعقوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r18.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r18.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiʿ says Abū ʿAmr avoids final qāf-to-kāf assimilation because the kāf is at the stopping point; partial or full articulation would violate customary stopping, while other readers may treat the ending as medial or avoid stopping.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p400/r18.anchor: قال صاحب اللوامح: وإنما امتنع أبو عمرو من إدغام مثله بعد إدغامه نرزقكم ونحوها لحلول الكاف منه طرفا وهو حرف وقف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r1.claim: After commanding the Prophet to pray, God tells him to command his household so they cooperate in relying on God amid scarcity, rather than fixating on livelihood or living luxuriously.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r1.anchor: أمر ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) أن يأمر أهله بالصلاة بعدما أمر هو عليه الصلاة والسلام بها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r2.claim: Reported referents include the Prophet's wives, daughters, and son-in-law; those relatives plus believing Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muṭṭalib; or all his followers. Al-Alusi favors his household.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r2.anchor: قيل أزواجه وبناته وصهره على رضى الله تعالى عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r3.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports that for eight months the Prophet came to ʿAlī's door at dawn prayer, urging prayer and invoking the purification of the People of the House; Imāmī reports likewise.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال : لما نزلت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r4.claim: Prayer here most likely means obligatory prayers; children should be commanded before obligation so they become accustomed to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بالصلاة الصلوات المفروضة ويؤمر بأدائها الصبي وإن لم تجب عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r5.speaker: أبو داود
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r5.claim: Abū Dāwūd transmits a sound-chain raised report: command children to pray at seven, discipline them for it at ten, and separate their beds.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r5.anchor: فقد روى أبو داود بإسناد حسن مرفوع مروا أولادكم بالصلاة وهم أبناء سبع سنين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r6.claim: Iṣṭabir means persist; patience stands metonymically for persistence, since it is a necessary accompaniment of persistence.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r6.anchor: أي وداوم عليها فالصبر مجاز مرسل عن المداومة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r7.claim: The wording indicates that fully observing worship is difficult for the soul; the address also extends to the household and, in what follows, more generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r7.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن العبادة في رعايتها حق الرعاية مشقة على النفس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r8.claim: The earlier command to glorify God, followed by prayer and a direct command to the Prophet to persist, signals his elevated rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r8.anchor: ما في التعبير بالتسبيح أولا والصلاة ثانيا مع توجيه الخطاب بالمداومة إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r9.claim: This reassures them that keeping prayer will not harm their livelihood: do not abandon prayer for earning, since God does not require them to provide for themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r9.anchor: دفع لما عسى أن يخطر ببال أحد من أن المداومة على الصلاة ربما تضر بأمر المعاش

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r10.claim: Fronting نحن either restricts the provision to God or adds emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r10.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه للاختصاص أو لإفادة التقوي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r11.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r11.claim: Some claim the command and ruling are specific to the Prophet; al-Alusi rejects the inference that a general address would license Muslims to abandon earning.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r11.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الخطاب خاص وكذا الحكم إذ لو كان عاما لرخص لكل مسلم المداومة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r12.claim: Generality only allows leaving work when it obstructs prayer; performing obligatory prayer is itself required, and persistence means praying at appointed times, not occupying all day and night.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r12.anchor: أن قصارى ما يلزم العموم سواء كان الأهل خاصا أو عاما لسائر المؤمنين أن يرخص للمصلي ترك الاكتساب المانع من الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r13.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r13.claim: A sound-chain report says the Prophet ordered his household to pray when hardship or distress came and recited this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r13.anchor: عن عبد الله بن سلام قال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r14.speaker: ثابت
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r14.claim: Thābit says the Prophet called his household to prayer when they faced scarcity; Thābit adds that prophets resorted to prayer when trouble came.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r15.speaker: أسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r15.claim: Aslam reports that ʿUmar prayed at night, then woke his household near its end for prayer and recited this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r15.anchor: وأخرج مالك والبيهقي عن اسلم قال كان عمر بن الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r16.claim: In light of these reports, prayer may be understood generally rather than restricted to obligatory prayers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r16.anchor: وجوز لظاهر الأخبار أن يراد بالصلاة مطلقها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r17.speaker: ابن وثاب ويعقوب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r17.claim: Ibn Waththāb and a group, also Yaʿqūb, assimilate the qāf into the kāf in نرزقك.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r18.speaker: السدى
ALUSI-FULL:v16p284#2/r18.claim: The good end is broader than Paradise and other outcomes; al-Suddī identifies it specifically as Paradise.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p285/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285/r1.claim: The phrase means the outcome belongs to the people of piety, with أهلها understood, as in 7:128; the implied noun may also be omitted, highlighting piety as the key.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p285/r1.anchor: أي لأهلها كما في قوله تعالى والعاقبة للمتقين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r1.claim: “Your family” means your people; another view means those who share your religion, as in Maryam 19:55.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r1.anchor: أي قومك. وقيل: من كان على دينك،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r2.claim: Persist in prayer, since prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r2.anchor: أي اصبر على الصلاة، فإنها تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r3.claim: God does not charge the Prophet with providing for any creature or even himself; He charges him with work.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r3.anchor: لا نكلفك أن ترزق أحدا من خلقنا، ولا أن ترزق نفسك وإنما نكلفك عملا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r4.claim: God provides for the Prophet and the good end is praiseworthy.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r5.claim: The good, praiseworthy end belongs to the people of piety.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r5.anchor: الخاتمة الجميلة المحمودة، {للتقوى} أي لأهل التقوى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the pious as those who affirm the Prophet, follow him, and fear God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الذين صدقوك واتبعوك واتقوني.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r7.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r7.claim: A report in some Musnads says that when hardship struck his family, the Prophet would order them to pray and recite this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p304/r7.anchor: وفي بعض المسانيد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "كان إذا أصاب أهله ضر أمرهم بالصلاة وتلا هذه الآية

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r2.claim: The command is for the Prophet to tell his household or followers to pray, so they can seek help with hardship and avoid preoccupation with livelihood or the habits of the wealthy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r2.anchor: أمره بأن يأمر أهل بيته أو التابعين له من أمته بالصلاة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r3.claim: Persist in prayer and keep it up.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r4.claim: God does not require the Prophet to provide for himself or his family; God provides for them so he can devote his attention to the afterlife.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r4.anchor: { لا نسألك رزقا } أي أن ترزق نفسك ولا أهلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r5.claim: The good outcome belongs to the people of piety.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r6.claim: A report says that when the Prophet's family suffered hardship, he would instruct them to pray and recite this verse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:132-133/r6.anchor: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان إذا أصاب أهله ضر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r1.claim: The author links prayer to the statement that prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing; he omits zakat here because the preceding verse already discourages worldly attachment.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r1.anchor: ولم يذكر الزكاة لدخولها في التزهيد بالآية التي قبلها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r2.claim: The iftiʿāl form of persevere conveys effort: devote yourself to prayer even when it occupies time that could go to livelihood.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r2.anchor: بصيغة الافتعال { عليها } أي على فعلها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r3.claim: God does not require the Prophet to earn provision for himself or others; divine majesty means He supplies what would otherwise distract him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r3.anchor: أي نكلفك طلبه لنفسك ولا لغيرك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r4.claim: God answers the worry about where provision will come from: He provides for the Prophet and his family from His boundless dominion, including through unexpected means.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r4.anchor: بنون العظمة { نرزقك } لك ولهم ما قدرناه لكم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r5.claim: People should not exhaust themselves chasing provision: neither diligence nor neglect can alter the amount allotted to each person from eternity.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r5.anchor: فإن كلا من الجاد فيه والمتهاون به لا يناله أكثر مما قسمناه له

BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r6.claim: Those who trust God and turn to Him live with contentment and ease; those who turn away and rely on their own effort remain in toil and distress, while the final good outcome belongs to the pious.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r6.anchor: فالمتقي لله المقبل على ذكره واثق بوعده انع راض

BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r7.claim: No concern about provision rivals prayer in importance.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r7.anchor: ولا معولة على الرزق وغيره توازي الصلاة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r8.speaker: حذيفة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r8.claim: Hudhayfa reports that when something troubled him, the Prophet resorted to prayer; Ahmad transmits the report and al-Baghawī cites it without a full chain at the end of al-Ḥijr.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r8.anchor: فزع إلى الصلاة - أخرجه أحمد عن حذيفة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r9.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām reports that when hardship came to the Prophet’s household, he ordered them to pray and recited this verse; al-Ṭabarānī says it is known only by this chain and Maʿmar alone transmitted it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r9.anchor: عن عبد الله بن سلام رضي الله عنه قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r10.speaker: ثابت
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r10.claim: Thābit reports that when the Messenger faced hardship, he called his family to pray; Thābit adds that prophets resorted to prayer when an affair distressed them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r10.anchor: عن ثابت قال : كان الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أصابته خصاصة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r11.claim: Abū Hurayra reports a divine saying promising inner richness and relief from poverty to one who devotes himself to worship, and preoccupation and unmet poverty otherwise; al-Tirmidhī grades it ḥasan gharīb.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p59/r11.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r8.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr understands “your family” as your people.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {وأمر أهلك بالصلاة} قال: قومك

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r9.speaker: سفيان الثوري
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r9.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī explains this as God not burdening the Prophet with seeking provision.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r9.anchor: عن سفيان الثوري في قوله: {لا نسألك رزقا} قال: لا نكلفك بالطلب

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r10.speaker: عروة
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r10.claim: ʿUrwa would recite the warning against coveting worldly goods after visiting the rich, then urge his household to keep up prayer.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r10.anchor: عن عروة أنه كان إذا دخل على أهل الدنيا فرأى من دنياهم طرفا فإذا رجع إلى أهله فدخل الدار قرأ {ولا تمدن عينيك} إلى قوله: {نحن نرزقك} ثم يقول: الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r11.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r11.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports that for eight months the Prophet came to ʿAlī’s door at dawn and called the household to prayer, reciting 33:33.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r11.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: لما نزلت {وأمر أهلك بالصلاة} كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يجيء إلى باب علي صلاة الغداة ثمانية أشهر

DURR-FULL:v5p612/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r12.speaker: ثابت
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r12.claim: Thābit reports that when the Prophet’s family faced hardship, he called them to prayer; he adds that prophets turned to prayer when trouble came.
DURR-FULL:v5p612/r12.anchor: عن ثابت قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أصابت أهله خصاصة نادى أهله بالصلاة: صلوا صلوا قال ثابت: وكانت الأنبياء إذا نزل بهم أمر فزعوا إلى الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v5p613/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r1.speaker: رجل من قريش
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r1.claim: A Qurashī narrator says the Prophet ordered his family to pray and recited this verse whenever household provision grew tight.
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن رجل من قريش قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دخل على أهله بعض الضيق في الرزق أمر أهله بالصلاة ثم قرأ {وأمر أهلك بالصلاة} الآية

DURR-FULL:v5p613/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, in a report the source grades sound, says the Prophet ordered his family to pray and recited this verse when hardship or shortage came upon them.
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r2.anchor: بسند صحيح عن عبد الله بن سلام قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزلت بأهله شدة أو ضيق أمرهم بالصلاة وتلا {وأمر أهلك بالصلاة} الآية

DURR-FULL:v5p613/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r3.claim: Aslam reports that ʿUmar prayed at night and woke his family near dawn, urging them to pray while reciting this verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r3.anchor: عن أسلم قال: كان عمر بن الخطاب يصلي من الليل ما شاء الله أن يصلي حتى إذا كان آخر الليل أيقظ أهله للصلاة ويقول لهم: الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v5p613/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r4.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r4.claim: ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr advised anyone dazzled by worldly adornment to return to their family, command prayer, and persevere, citing the verse’s warning against coveting such goods.
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r4.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة قال: قال لنا أبي: إذا رأى أحدكم شيئا من زينة الدنيا وزهرتها فليأت أهله وليأمر أهله بالصلاة وليصطبر عليها

DURR-FULL:v5p613/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r5.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r5.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the good end promised to the God-fearing as Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v5p613/r5.anchor: عن السدي في وله {والعاقبة للتقوى} قال: هي الجنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r1.claim: Ahl answers the preceding mention of spouses: the Prophet and his family are to find their enjoyment in prayer rather than worldly decoration; a man’s family is his most exemplary dependents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r1.anchor: ذكر الأهل هنا مقابل لذكر الأزواج في قوله { إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم } ( طه : 131 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r2.claim: Al-Bukhari reports that Fatima sought a captive servant because grinding exhausted her; the Prophet told her and Ali that tasbih, tahmid, and takbir, each thirty-three times after prayer, was better than a servant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r2.anchor: فأخبرت عائشة بذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فجاءها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد أخذت وعلي مضجعهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r3.claim: God commands the Messenger to persevere in prayer even more than he commands his family; iṣṭibār means restraint and figuratively means abundant voluntary prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r3.anchor: وأمر الله رسوله بما هو أعظم مما يأمر به أهله وهو أن يصطبر على الصلاة . والاصطبار : الانحباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r4.claim: The sentence is parenthetical between the command and the assurance that God provides.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r4.anchor: وجملة { لا نسألك رزقا } معترضة بين التي قبلها وبين جملة { نحن نرزقك } جعلت تمهيدا لهاته الأخيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r5.claim: God requires worship alone, as gratitude for His favor, not payment; this refutes the taxes and tribute people customarily pay rulers and tribal or military leaders.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r5.anchor: أي ما كلفناك إلا بالعبادة ، لأن العبادة شكر لله على ما تفضل به على الخلق ولا يطلب الله منهم جزاء آخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r6.claim: God’s assurance that He provides explains the preceding verse’s promise that the Lord’s provision is better and lasting: that provision is directed to the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p342#2/r6.anchor: فجملة { نحن نرزقك } مبينة لجملة { ورزق ربك خير وأبقى } ( طه : 131 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r1.claim: The address first concerns the Prophet, but includes his household and believers because the reason for the command applies to all Muslims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r1.anchor: والمقصود من هذا الخطاب ابتداء هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويشمل أهله والمؤمنين لأن المعلل به هذه الجملة مشترك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r2.claim: The statement is coordinated with God’s not asking for provision and explains perseverance in prayer: what is required is piety, whose end is good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r2.anchor: وجملة { والعاقبة للتقوى } عطف على جملة { لا نسألك رزقا } المعلل بها أمره بالاصطبار للصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r3.claim: ʿĀqibah is whatever follows an affair, good or bad, though common usage favors a good outcome; piety ultimately yields good outcomes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r3.anchor: وحقيقة العاقبة : أنها كل ما يعقب أمرا ويقع في آخره من خير وشر ، إلا أنها غلب استعمالها في أمور الخير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r4.claim: The lām marks possession and confirms the intended good outcome; this holds absolutely for the hereafter and may also hold for worldly good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r4.anchor: واللام للملك تحقيقا لإرادة الخير من العاقبة لأن شأن لام الملك أن تدل على نوال الأمر المرغوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r5.claim: As a universal coda, the sentence means that the outcome belongs only to the pious and has the force of a proverb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p343/r5.anchor: وهذه الجملة تذييل لما فيها من معنى العموم ، أي لا تكون العاقبة إلا للتقوى . فهذه الجملة أرسلت مجرى المثل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r13.claim: The Prophet is to command his family to pray, model prayer with them, and persevere in it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r13.anchor: ثم أمره تعالى بأن يأمر أهله بالصلاة وتمثيلها معهم ويصطبر عليها ويلازمها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r14.claim: God alone undertakes the Prophet’s provision, so prayer and perseverance do not make him responsible for securing it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r14.anchor: ويصطبر عليها ويلازمها ويتكفل هو برزقه لا إله إلا هو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r15.claim: The ultimate outcome belongs to piety, bringing God’s victory in this world and mercy in the next.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r15.anchor: وأخبره أن العاقبة الأولى التقوى وفي حيزها فثم نصر الله في الدنيا ورحمته في الآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r16.claim: Although addressed to the Prophet, the instruction includes his whole community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r16.anchor: وهذا الخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، ويدخل في عمومه جميع أمته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r18.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r18.claim: ʿUmar would wake his household for night prayer, pray himself, and invoke this verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r18.anchor: وكان عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يوقظ أهل داره لصلاة الليل ويصلي هو ويتمثل بهذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r19.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r19.claim: The majority read narzuquka with a ḍamma on the qāf.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r20.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70#2/r20.claim: A group reads the qāf of narzuquka as still.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r1.claim: He explains commanding one's family to pray as rescuing them from God's punishment through prayer, and says one must persevere in it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r2.claim: Aslam recounts that ʿUmar kept a nightly prayer time and, when he awoke to pray, roused his household citing this command.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r2.anchor: أن عمر بن الخطاب كان يبيت عنده أنا ويرفأ، وكان له ساعة من الليل يصلي فيها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r3.claim: Establishing prayer brings provision from where one does not expect; he connects this promise to God's provision for the Godfearing and to humanity's purpose of worship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r3.anchor: يعني (9) إذا أقمت الصلاة أتاك الرزق من حيث لا تحتسب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r4.speaker: الثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r4.claim: Al-Thawrī glosses the phrase to mean that God does not charge the Prophet with seeking provision.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r4.anchor: وقال الثوري: {لا نسألك رزقا} أي: لا نكلفك الطلب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r5.speaker: أبوه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r5.claim: Hishām's father would recite these verses after seeing worldly wealth, then urge his own household to pray.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r5.anchor: عن هشام، عن أبيه؛ أنه كان إذا دخل على أهل الدنيا، فرأى من دنياهم طرفا فإذا رجع إلى أهله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r6.claim: Thābit reports that when hardship struck the Prophet, he called his family to pray repeatedly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r6.anchor: عن ثابت قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أصابه خصاصة نادى أهله: " يا أهلاه، صلوا، صلوا "

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r7.speaker: ثابت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r7.claim: Thābit adds that prophets resorted to prayer whenever an urgent matter came upon them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r7.anchor: قال ثابت: وكانت (1) الأنبياء إذا نزل بهم (2) أمر فزعوا إلى الصلاة. (3)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r8.speaker: الله تعالى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r8.claim: In a divine report narrated by Abū Hurayra, God promises to fill with richness and relieve poverty whoever devotes themself to worship, while neglect leaves them busy and poor.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p327/r8.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " يقول الله تعالى: يا ابن آدم تفرغ لعبادتي أملأ صدرك غنى، وأسد فقرك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports the Prophet's teaching that making the Hereafter one's single concern suffices for worldly worries, while scattered worldly concerns leave one exposed to ruin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r1.anchor: سمعت نبيكم صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " من جعل الهموم هما واحدا هم المعاد كفاه الله هم دنياه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Thābit reports that worldly obsession brings disarray and poverty, whereas intending the Hereafter brings order, inward wealth, and worldly provision in spite of itself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r2.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " من كانت الدنيا همه فرق الله عليه أمره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r3.claim: The good end belongs to the Godfearing in this world and the next, culminating in Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r3.anchor: وحسن العاقبة في الدنيا والآخرة، وهي الجنة، لمن اتقى الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r4.claim: In an authentic report, the Prophet interprets dates from Ibn Ṭāb in a dream as foretelling the believers' good outcome in this world, elevation, and the soundness of their religion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p328/r4.anchor: وفي الصحيح: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " رأيت الليلة كأنا في دار عقبة بن رافع

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r24.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r24.claim: Ahlak can mean the Prophet's household and his community of faith.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r24.anchor: وأمر أهلك قيل: أهل بيتك وأهل دينك بالصلاة واصطبر عليها

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r25.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r25.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r25.claim: The instruction is to persevere in performing prayer.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r25.anchor: واصطبر عليها أي: على فعلها لا نسألك رزقا أي: لا نسألك

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r26.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r26.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r26.claim: God does not ask the Prophet for something that benefits God, as worldly kings extract benefits; instead, the commanded work benefits the person who does it.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r26.anchor: لا نسألك رزقا أي: لا نسألك شيئا ينتفع به كما يفعله ملوك الدنيا من جر المنافع، وإنما نكلفك العمل

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r27.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r27.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r27.claim: God does not assign the Prophet or his household the task of providing their livelihood; He assigns worship and conveying the message, and guarantees everyone's provision.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r27.anchor: وقيل: لا نكلفك رزقك ورزق عيالك؛ بل كلفناك العبادة وأداء الرسالة، وضمنّا رزق الجميع

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r28.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r28.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r28.claim: The phrase means that God gives the Prophet provision.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r28.anchor: نحن نرزقك أي: نعطيك والعاقبة للتقوى أي: العاقبة المحمودة

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r29.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r29.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r29.claim: The praiseworthy final outcome belongs to the Godfearing.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r29.anchor: والعاقبة للتقوى أي: العاقبة المحمودة لأهل التقوى

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r30.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r30.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r30.claim: Another explanation likens the final outcome to a market in which only piety is of value, so the outcome belongs to it.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r30.anchor: وقيل: لا ينفق في سوق العاقبة إلا التقوى فكان العاقبة له، وعن هشام

JISHUMI:v7p4771/r31.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r31.speaker: هشام بن عروة بن الزبير
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r31.claim: Hisham reports that when Urwa ibn al-Zubayr saw the rulers' possessions, he went home, recited these verses, and called people to prayer.
JISHUMI:v7p4771/r31.anchor: وعن هشام بن عروة بن الزبير قال: كان عروة بن الزبير إذا رأى ما عند السلطان دخل بيته

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r12.claim: “Your family” may mean the Prophet's relatives by lineage.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r13.claim: Alternatively, it may mean everyone who followed and believed in him, since obedience makes them like his family.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r13.anchor: جميع من اتبعه وآمن به , لأنهم يحلون بالطاعة له محل أهله

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r14.claim: The command is to persevere in performing prayer and in enjoining it on one's family.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r14.anchor: اصبر على فعلها وعلى أمرهم بها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r15.claim: Though addressed to the Prophet, the assurance applies to all creatures: God provides for them without needing provision and benefits them without receiving benefit, emphasizing His favor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r15.anchor: فالمراد به جميع الخلق أنه تعالى يرزقهم ولا يسترزقهم , وينفعهم ولا ينتفع بهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p433/r16.claim: The good outcome belongs to the people of piety.

MUQATIL:20:132/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:132/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:132/r1.claim: “Your family” means your people, as in the statement about Abraham commanding his family in 19:55.

MUQATIL:20:132/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:132/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:132/r2.claim: The command is to pray and persist in prayer.

MUQATIL:20:132/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:132/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:132/r3.claim: God does not ask people for provision; what He asks of them is worship, and He provides for them.
MUQATIL:20:132/r3.anchor: مآ أريد منهم من رزق ومآ أريد أن يطعمون

MUQATIL:20:132/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:132/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:132/r4.claim: The outcome of God-consciousness is the Garden.

MUQATIL:20:132/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:132/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:132/r5.claim: The claim that God seeks worship, not provision, is linked to 51:56–57, where creation is for worship and God asks no provision or food.
MUQATIL:20:132/r5.anchor: وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون مآ أريد منهم من رزق ومآ أريد أن يطعمون

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r3.claim: The Prophet is commanded to keep his household or community at prayer and personally persist in it.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r4.speaker: author
