NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r4.claim: God does not ask the Prophet to provide for himself or his family; God provides for them, so he should focus on worship and the afterlife.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r4.anchor: أي لا نسألك ان ترزق نفسك ولا اهلك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r5.claim: Nasafi adds that whoever is occupied with God's work is cared for by God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r5.anchor: لأن من كان في عمل الله كان الله في عمله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r6.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r6.claim: When he saw what the rulers possessed, ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr recited the preceding warning against coveting worldly goods, then called people to prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r6.anchor: وعن عروة بن الزبير أنه كان إذا رأى ما عند السلاطين فرأ ولا تمدن عينيك الآية ثم ينادي الصلاة الصلاة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r7.speaker: بكر بن عبد الله المزني
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r7.claim: When his family faced hardship, Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzanī told them to rise and pray, citing God's command.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r7.anchor: وكان بكر بن عبد الله المزني إذا أصاب أهله خصاصة قال قوموا فصلوا بهذا أمر الله ورسوله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r8.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r8.claim: A report in some musnads, related from Malik ibn Dinar, says the Prophet ordered his family to pray and recited this verse when hardship struck them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r8.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار مثله في بعض المسانيد انه عليه السلام كان اذا اصاب اهله ضرا أمرهم بالصلاة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r9.claim: The phrase means that the good outcome belongs to the Godfearing, with two annexed nouns elided.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72#3/r9.anchor: أي وحسن العاقبة لأهل التقوى بحذف المضافين

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r8.claim: God commands the Prophet to order his family to pray, to pray with them himself, and to persevere; the address includes the whole community, with his household specially included.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r8.anchor: أمره تعالى بأن يأمر أهله بالصلاة ويمتثلها معهم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r9.claim: After this verse was revealed, the Prophet went each morning to Fatima and Ali's home and called them to prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r9.anchor: وكان عليه السلام بعد نزول هذه الآية يذهب كل صباح إلى بيت فاطمة وعلي رضوان الله عليهما

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r10.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r10.claim: When Urwa ibn al-Zubayr saw reports about rulers, he hurried home, recited the verse through wa-abqā, called his household to prayer, and prayed.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r10.anchor: ويروى أن عروة بن الزبير رضي الله عنه كان إذا رأى شيئا من أخبار السلاطين وأحوالهم بادر إلى منزله فدخله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r11.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r11.claim: Umar ibn al-Khattab woke his household for night prayer, prayed, and invoked this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r11.anchor: وكان عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يوقظ أهل داره لصلاة الليل ويصلي

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r12.claim: God does not ask the Prophet to provide for himself and his family or neglect prayer for income; God guarantees their provision, and in household hardship the Prophet told them to pray.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#2/r12.anchor: لا نسألك أن ترزق نفسك وإياهم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#3/r2.claim: The good end for the God-fearing is Paradise; others may have an outcome, but it is blameworthy and so as if nonexistent.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:131-132#3/r2.anchor: أي الجنة لأهل التقوى يعني العاقبة المحمودة

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r1.claim: The poor should use prayer to face poverty rather than worry over livelihood or look toward the wealthy.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r1.anchor: يعني : كما أمرناك بالصلاة فأمر أنت أهل بيتك فإن الفقير ينبغي أن يستعين بها

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r2.claim: The Prophet used to visit Fāṭima and ʿAlī each morning for months and call them to prayer.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r2.anchor: فكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يذهب إلى فاطمة وعلي كل صباح

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r3.speaker: عرائس البقلي
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r3.claim: ʿArāʾis al-Baqli identifies istibār as the station of struggle and patience as the station of witnessing.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r3.anchor: قال في "عرائس البقلى" : الاصطبار مقام المجاهدة والصبر مقام المشاهدة

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ calls istibār the hardest patience: the heart and inner self remain still under trials, while ordinary patience is of the lower self.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطاء أشد أنواع الصبر الاصطبار وهو السكون تحت موارد البلاء بالسر والقلب

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r5.claim: God does not ask the Prophet to provide for himself or his family; He asks him to worship.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r5.anchor: أي : لا نكلفك أن ترزق نفسك ولا أهلك إنما نسألك العبادة

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r6.claim: God provides for the Prophet and his family, freeing his attention for the afterlife; those serving God receive His care.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r6.anchor: وإياهم ففرغ بالك لأمر الآخرة فإن من كان في عمل الله كان الله في عمله

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r7.claim: When unqualified, al-ʿāqibah denotes the praiseworthy final reward, Paradise.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r7.anchor: الحميدة وهي الجنة فإن إطلاقها يختص بالثواب

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r8.claim: The good end belongs to the God-fearing, meaning the Prophet and his followers; taqwā restrains soul and limbs from what knowledge condemns.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r8.anchor: وهو ذم النفس والجوارح عن جميع ما يقبحه العلم

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r9.claim: When hardship struck his household, the Prophet commanded them to pray and recited this verse.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r9.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام كان إذا أصاب أهله ضر أمرهم بالصلاة وتلا هذه الآية

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r10.speaker: وهب بن منبه
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r10.claim: Wahb says needs are not sought from God by anything like prayer; earlier believers turned to it in crises and often found relief.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r10.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه : إن الحوائج لم تطلب من الله تعالى بمثل الصلاة

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Jonah was among those who prayed; otherwise he would have remained in the fish until resurrection.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r11.anchor: يعني من المصلين للبث في بطنه إلى يوم يبعثون

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r12.speaker: الشافعي
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r12.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī draws from the verse that glorification is the most beneficial remedy for an epidemic.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r12.anchor: وعن الشافعي رحمه الله أخذا من هذه الآية لم أر أنفع للوباء من التسبيح

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r13.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r13.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh pictures prayer and fasting as warp and weft of worshippers’ robes; bodily prayer is obligatory and voluntary prayer, while the soul’s prayer rises toward spiritual nearness.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r13.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ رحمه الله للعابدين أردية يكسونها من عند الله سداها الصلاة ولحمتها الصوم

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r14.claim: In Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh’s taxonomy, the heart’s prayer is lasting vigilance and presence, and the secret’s prayer is turning from all but God in witnessing.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r14.anchor: وصلاة القلب دوام المراقبة ولزوم المحاضرة كقوله :

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r15.claim: The spirit’s prayer is annihilation in God and abiding through God, exemplified by obedience to the Messenger.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r15.anchor: وصلاة الروح فناؤه في الله وبقاؤه بالله

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r16.claim: Those who attain these forms of prayer are freed from dependence on people and receive God’s provision, as the Prophet’s life illustrates.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r16.anchor: فمن صلى هذه الصلاة أغناه الله عما عند الناس ورزقه مما عنده

BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r17.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r17.claim: The Prophet says he spends the night with his Lord, who feeds and gives him drink.
BURSEVI:v5p344#2/r17.anchor: كان يقول صلى الله عليه وسلم "أبيت عند ربي يطعمني ويسقيني"
